name: UK grocery basket: weekly EAN price monitor

nodes.name: Settings
nodes.notes: The one node you edit: the EAN list (one per line), the alert threshold in percent, the Google Sheet and tab for the history, and the email address the alerts go to.

nodes.name: Valid basket?
nodes.notes: True: send the request. False: email the problem (no valid EAN, or more than 200).

nodes.name: Price the basket
nodes.notes: Header Auth credential: name Authorization, value Bearer then a space then your Apify token. Error answers come back as data on purpose, so the next node can explain them.

nodes.name: Answer ok?
nodes.notes: True: carry on to the sheet. False: email the problem with the reason.

nodes.name: Read history
nodes.notes: Reads every row of the history tab. Always outputs one item, so an empty tab (first run) still carries on.

nodes.name: Week not recorded yet?
nodes.notes: True: append this week's rows. False: the week is already in the sheet, so nothing is added twice. Keep this branch above Anything moved? so the history is saved before any email is sent.

nodes.name: Append this week
nodes.notes: Appends the rows to the bottom of the history tab, matching columns by the names in the header row. Cell format is RAW: values are stored as typed text, so a value starting with an equals sign can never become a formula and EAN leading zeros are kept.

nodes.name: Anything moved?
nodes.notes: True: at least one price moved by the threshold or an item is no longer priced. False: nothing to say, so no email (quiet weeks and the first baseline run).

nodes.name: Email the movers
nodes.notes: Gmail node (OAuth2). Any other channel works: swap this node for Slack, SMTP Send Email or Telegram; the message fields are $json.subject, $json.html and $json.text.

nodes.name: Email a problem
nodes.notes: Plain-text email with the reason and what to do. Swap for Slack if you prefer: use $json.text, or $json.error for a step that failed.

parameters.message: ={{ $json.text || ('A step of the workflow failed: ' + (($json.error && $json.error.message) || $json.error || 'no detail') + '. Open the failed execution in n8n to see which step. Common causes: the Google Sheets credential, the sheet id or the tab name in Settings, or a header row that does not match the README.') }}
parameters.subject: ={{ 'Weekly EAN price monitor needs attention: ' + ($json.headline || 'a step failed') }}

parameters.content:
## Weekly EAN price monitor

Prices a fixed list of EANs at Tesco, Sainsbury's, Asda and Aldi once a week, adds the prices to a Google Sheet as history, compares them with the previous week and alerts you only about items that moved by more than your threshold.

Prices come from the Actor's weekly snapshot (live is off). The index is rebuilt on Sundays, so a Monday run reads fresh data.

**Set up:** fill in Settings, add the three credentials (Header Auth for Apify, Google Sheets, Gmail), give the sheet its header row (see the README), run once by hand to record the baseline, then activate.

**Cost:** EANs x retailers x $0.002 per week at most (only matched lines are charged), plus your own Apify Standby compute. Example: 20 EANs at 4 retailers is at most $0.16 a week.

**Slack:** swap either Gmail node for a Slack Send a message node. The movers text is $json.text; a problem has $json.reason and $json.action.

**Failures elsewhere:** set an Error Workflow in the workflow settings.

## Every Monday 08:00
**What it does:** starts the workflow once a week. The Actor rebuilds its price index every Sunday, so Monday morning is the first time the new prices are ready. Running it more often only returns the same prices and charges you again.
**Change:** the day and time, and your n8n timezone.
**Cost:** none.

## Settings
**What it does:** the one node you edit.
- standbyUrl: the Actor's public Standby address (the same for everyone)
- eans: one per line, 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits, at most 200
- thresholdPct: alert when a price moves this many % or more, up or down
- sheetDocumentId, sheetName: the Google Sheet and tab that hold the history
- alertTo: who gets the emails
- includeLoyalty: true compares Clubcard and Nectar prices when they are lower

**Change:** replace the placeholders.
**Cost:** every EAN you add costs up to 4 x $0.002 a week.

## Build basket request
**What it does:** trims the list, keeps numbers of 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits, removes duplicates and refuses more than 200. Builds the request body with live: false. If nothing valid is left it goes to the problem email instead of calling Apify.
**Change:** rarely. The code lives in src/build-request.js.
**Cost:** none.

## Valid basket?
**What it does:** true sends the request. false sends the problem email with the reason (no valid EAN, or too many).
**Change:** nothing.
**Cost:** none.

## Price the basket
**What it does:** POST to your standbyUrl + /basket with your Apify token (Header Auth credential, value Bearer then a space then the token). Waits up to 300 s. An error answer comes back as data, not as a workflow error, so the next step can explain it.
**Change:** the credential, and standbyUrl in Settings.
**Cost:** $0.002 per matched line per retailer, so EANs x retailers x $0.002 a week at most, plus your own Standby compute.

## Check the answer
**What it does:** turns the status into ok or a problem with a plain reason: 400 invalid, 401/403 token, 402 spend limit, 429 busy, 503 index or charging, 504 timeout, with Retry-After when sent. Prices more than 10 days old count as a problem (the weekly snapshot may have failed). A retailer that is down is only a warning.
**Change:** rarely. The code lives in src/check-answer.js.
**Cost:** none.

## Answer ok?
**What it does:** true carries on to the sheet. false sends the problem email.
**Change:** nothing.
**Cost:** none.

## Flatten prices
**What it does:** one row per matched line per retailer, in the order of the sheet header row. effectivePrice is the loyalty price when includeLoyalty is on and it is lower. Also collects the EANs that matched nowhere, for the alert.
**Change:** if you add a column, add it to the sheet header too. The code lives in src/flatten-prices.js.
**Cost:** none.

## Read history
**What it does:** reads every row of the history tab. An empty tab is fine on the first run. A failure here (credential, sheet id, tab name) goes to the problem email.
**Change:** the Google Sheets credential; sheetDocumentId and sheetName in Settings.
**Cost:** none (Google API quota only).

## Compare with last week
**What it does:** for each retailer and EAN, finds the latest earlier week in the history and works out the % change in effectivePrice. Movers change by thresholdPct or more. Only compares a retailer and EAN when both weeks matched the same retailer product; a product that changed is listed on its own, not as a move. Also lists items priced last week but not now, marks a week that is already in the sheet (nothing is appended twice), and on a first run records a baseline with no alerts.
**Change:** thresholdPct in Settings. The code lives in src/compare-weeks.js.
**Cost:** none.

## Week not recorded yet?
**What it does:** true goes on to append this week's rows. false (the week is already in the sheet) skips it. This branch sits above the alert branch on purpose: n8n runs the top branch first, so the history is saved before any email goes out.
**Change:** nothing. Keep it above Anything moved?.
**Cost:** none.

## Split rows to append
**What it does:** turns the list of rows into one item per row, ready for the Google Sheets node.
**Change:** nothing.
**Cost:** none.

## Append this week
**What it does:** adds the rows to the bottom of the history tab, matching columns by the header names.
**Change:** the header row must be exactly the columns listed in the README. Keep the Cell Format option on RAW: values are stored as text, so nothing from a retailer can become a formula and EAN leading zeros survive.
**Cost:** none. A failure goes to the problem email.

## Anything moved?
**What it does:** true when at least one price moved by the threshold or an item is no longer priced. false ends quietly, so quiet weeks and the first (baseline) run send nothing.
**Change:** nothing.
**Cost:** none.

## Email the movers
**What it does:** an HTML table of the movers, then the items no longer priced, the items now matched to a different product, the EANs not found and any retailer that could not be priced. The subject says how many moved and the week.
**Change:** alertTo in Settings and the Gmail credential. For Slack, replace this node with Slack Send a message and use $json.text.
**Cost:** none.

## Email a problem
**What it does:** a plain-text email with the reason and what to do. Reached from a bad EAN list, a bad answer, and errors in Flatten prices, Read history, Compare with last week or Append this week.
**Change:** alertTo in Settings and the Gmail credential. For Slack use $json.text, or $json.error for a step that failed.
**Cost:** none.
